newsitem.title: THAILAND: BAHT SEEN MOVING LITTLE AS FORWARDS FALL DUE.
newsitem.headline: BAHT SEEN MOVING LITTLE AS FORWARDS FALL DUE.

text.p: The Thai baht should move little as three month baht/dollar forward contracts held by fund managers mature on Friday, dealers said.
The forward contracts, estimated by dealers at a combined $1-4 billion, were taken out by speculators who shorted the baht in mid-May when they attacked the currency.
The baht was subsequently floated on July 2 and has since depreciated around 20 percent against the dollar.
The baht was quoted at 31.50/31.60 per dollar in the local market on Thursday afternoon against 25.90 prior to its flotation. In the offshore market, the baht was quoted at 31.40/31.60.
"I think this issue has been very much discounted by the market," said a dealer in Singapore.

"People said the baht would be affected by one month contracts maturing in June and by the two months in July but the effect then was pretty minimal. I would expect to see something similar tomorrow," he said.

An accumulation of baht by speculators to meet contract obligations may have offered some support to the currency this week in the face of regional currency weakness but the effects were limited, dealers said.

"I think the baht has turned a little bullish in the very short term on the IMF news. People looking for baht to meet these contracts may have helped a bit but it was only one factor," said a dealer at a local bank.

"I think the market is really looking at the regional currency issues. If you look at spot rates in offshore and onshore markets, they are very close. It would suggest they are still playing with the baht like other currencies in the region," said a dealer at a foreign bank onshore. ($1 = 31 baht)
